judged_text: On the sync path the function returns the raw fetch Response object, but all eight call sites dereference provider-native response shapes (Google reads res?.data, Hubspot reads .expires_in, Zoho reads .data.error, Lark/Webex/Zoom pass it to provider-specific error handlers expecting provider envelopes). With sharing and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT configured, every token refresh crashes or stores garbage: Google throws TypeError reading .access_token of undefined (Response has no .data), Zoho throws reading .error of undefined, Hubspot stores a NaN expiry and undefined access_token — the credential-sync path is unusable as written.

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` (new file `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns the raw `fetch(...)` Response when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy. Multiple updated call sites treat the return value as a provider-native/axios-like object (e.g. Google: `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` in `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`; Hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object; Zoho uses `tokenInfo.data...`; Lark/Webex/Zoom pass the result into handlers that expect parsed bodies). A `Response` has no `.data` and must be `.json()`'d, so with sync enabled these paths will either throw or propagate unusable values, making the credential-sync refresh path broken as written.
